Bitcoin on Thursday traded virtually unchanged, with investors contending with an unexpected lull following the conclusion of the popular multiday Consensus conference.
Consensus, in the recent past, has tended to provide a lift to the price of the No. 1 digital currency, one that hasnt materialized, so far.
Its still looking a bit soft and vulnerable, said Craig Erlam, senior market analyst at Oanda. Given that its a sentiment-driven market and things have been so quiet it wouldnt surprise me if we saw it head below $8,000.
Erlam added that he doesnt expect the bottom to fall out of bitcoin.
A single bitcoin BTCUSD, -1.29% last traded at $8,264.05, down 0.4%, since Wednesdays levels at 5 p.m. Eastern time on the Kraken exchange.

Apple co-founder endorses blockchain technology
Speaking at the WeAreDevelopers World Congress in Austria, Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.59% co-founder Steve Wozniak said blockchain, the distributed ledger that underpins cryptocurrencies, is the next major IT revolution that is about to happen, per the German outlet of Cointelegraph. Wozniak added that the technology would achieve full potential in a decade.
These arent the first pro-digital technology comments from Wozniak. At the Money conference in October, the tech genius said bitcoin is mathematically better than the U.S. dollar and gold because of the finite number of bitcoins that can be mined.

JPMorgan latest bank to explore crypto
JPMorgan Chase & Co JPM, -0.48% is the latest bank reportedly to be exploring the world of digital assets. According to a report from Financial News, the bank has appointed Oliver Harris to a role that is focused on cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology.
The news follows the May 2 announcement from Goldman Sachs Group GS, -0.67% that it is opening a cryptocurrency trading desk. The move into mainstream financial firms is further affirmation that Wall Street is committed to profiting from the rising popularity of nascent digital assets.

Altcoins and futures subdued start to Thursday
Coins other than bitcoin, known as altcoins, have drifted lower Thursday. Ether ETHUSD, -1.65% has lost 0.1% to $693.65, Bitcoin Cash BCHUSD, -3.22% is off 1.4% at $1,248.80, Litecoin LTCUSD, -2.73% is down 0.8% at $136.92 and Ripples XRP XRPUSD, -1.38% last traded at 68 cents, down 0.4%.
Futures have had a subdued Thursday. The Cboe June contract XBTM8, -0.97% has added 0.1% at $8,275, while the CME May contract BTCK8, -1.09% is unchanged at $8,250.
